notes.finding: Host-first preparation returned SELECTOR_INVALID_RESPONSE. No task tool was selected or executed; the agent explained the failure. Counted as a failed selection/execution, with usage retained.
The binary selector returned no_match. No business tool was executed. Aggregate telemetry cannot distinguish all-negative verdicts from a single insufficiently confident positive.

The selector chose list_integration_connections correctly, but the agent supplied a different operation ID to execute_read_action. The local store rejected it as OPERATION_NOT_FOUND. Selection and execution grades intentionally differ.

The expected get_flow handler ran, followed by additional get_woku work. The agent reached the fixed eight-turn limit before a final answer. Handler success is retained, final-answer completion is false.

The first create_flow attempt included the word woku inside an ID string. The native handler rejected that invalid ID before the creation command. A fresh operation with the correct bare ID succeeded. Both invocations and their cost remain counted; final state contains the baseline flow and exactly one new flow.

17 cases started with a non-reference business read after optional guide discovery, but all 60 eventually executed the reference handler. Those strict first-reference misses are not evidence of 17 unsafe or failed tasks.

Seven cases differ from the strict complete-argument oracle, mostly through additional query defaults or limits. Tool selection, exact arguments and handler success remain separate; no grading was relaxed after measurement.
25 first preparations were ambiguous; all included the reference tool. The agent resolved among those candidates without another Jev inference.

Three SELECTOR_INVALID_RESPONSE errors were followed by fresh agent-requested preparations. The expected handlers eventually ran; all attempts remain in latency, Jev usage, cost and MCP-error totals. The first-reference metric concerns an accepted tool proposal, not the first inference attempt.
